evals.prompt: I have a shopping assistant agent in Agent Studio and I want to run an evaluation on it to see how good it is. How do I do that from the CLI?
evals.expected_output: Uses algobot evals: metrics list to pick metric UUIDs, experiments create with index-name/agent-uuid/metric-ids/num-cases, poll experiments get, then runs summary and runs judgments to read results. Mentions the algobot-ai >= 2.1.0 version gate and that each case costs a real completion.
assertions: Uses algobot evals commands (metrics list, experiments create, runs summary)
Explains experiments are asynchronous and must be polled
Mentions cost: each case is a real completion plus judge calls
Notes the algobot-ai >= 2.1.0 version gate for the evals command group

evals.prompt: My production shopping agent scores badly on tone and faithfulness evals. Can you improve its settings automatically?
evals.expected_output: Proposes the clone-based tuning loop: keep the production agent untouched, clone it via scaffold + create (2.1.0+ scaffold strips deprecated config fields and captures providerId), keep the clone as draft (evals work on unpublished agents), run a baseline eval on the original, tune the clone, re-run on the same dataset, compare before/after, and only promote to the production agent after showing the diff and getting explicit approval.
assertions: Does NOT modify the production agent directly without explicit approval
Clones the agent (scaffold + create) and keeps the clone in draft
Runs a baseline eval on the original and compares candidate runs against it (same dataset)
Maps tone failures to an OUTPUT STYLE instruction contract and faithfulness failures to accuracy instructions or tool returned fields
Requires showing the config diff and explicit user approval before promoting/publishing

evals.prompt: I want to create evaluation cases from my agent's real conversation history instead of synthetic generated cases, so the eval reflects actual user traffic. How do I do that?
evals.expected_output: Walks through the real-history import recipe: extract conversations (conversations list/get --agent-id, mind the --page long form and --jq quote stripping), transform each user turn into an import row (prior turns verbatim as messages, served responses dropped, parts[] flattened to content, PII scrubbed, evalcase-/eval-experiment_run_ artifacts filtered out), build profiles, then datasets import with --validate-only before --auto-finalize, and pilot small before a full run.
assertions: Captures inputs only (query + prior turns) and drops the served response
Includes PII scrubbing before import (imported cases are visible in the dashboard)
Filters out previous eval-run artifacts (evalcase- messageIds, eval-experiment_run_ conversations) and technical test conversations
Uses datasets import with --validate-only first, then the atomic import
Warns to paginate with the long-form --page flag, not -p

evals.prompt: I ran a baseline eval on Agent A and then on Agent B (same index) with tone, faithfulness and relevance. Agent B scored 0 on tone even though its prompt asks for an energetic voice. I want 100 cases per metric for the next round. What should I run, and can I compare the two runs?
evals.expected_output: Explains that --num-cases is a TOTAL split evenly across metrics, so 3 metrics x 100 each means --num-cases 300. Applies the dataset provenance gate: without --dataset-id, experiments create was observed to resolve to an existing dataset for the same index built for another agent, so Agent B likely inherited Agent A's tone contract. Prints a run card (dataset id, agentProfileId, indexProfileId, cases per metric, distinct tone contracts), reviews the tone contracts against Agent B's voice, always passes --dataset-id, and refuses to compare runs on different datasets.
assertions: States that --num-cases is a total across metrics and gives --num-cases 300 for 3 metrics x 100
Identifies the missing --dataset-id / resolve-or-create dataset as the likely cause of the tone score
Prints or asks for a run card with dataset id, agent and index profile ids, cases per metric and tone contracts
Reviews the tone contract against the agent's voice instructions before trusting the tone score
Refuses to compare runs from different datasets and passes --dataset-id on every compared run

evals.prompt: My agent fails the tone metric on most cases and the judge reasons say the answer contains logs, tool calls and raw data. The agent ends its turn with a display tool that shows grouped product results. Should I rewrite the OUTPUT STYLE section of the prompt?
evals.expected_output: Runs the instrument check before touching the prompt: takes 2 failing cases from runs case, compares completion.responseText (what the user reads) with completion.answerText (observed in runs case output to also carry display-tool argument values), and re-judges the clean responseText with algobot evals judge (nothing stored). If the clean text passes, treats the failures as an instrument artifact rather than an agent defect, does not tune prompts against it, and reports it. Notes relevance appeared to grade displayed values by design (observed) and that skew on other metrics is not measured.
assertions: Does NOT immediately rewrite the prompt; runs the instrument check first
Compares completion.responseText with completion.answerText from runs case
Re-judges the clean text with algobot evals judge --metric-slug tone
Classifies log/tool-call/raw-data reasons with a clean visible answer as an instrument artifact, not an agent defect
Labels the behavior as observed (experimental endpoints), not a guaranteed property of the service
